goal: Worker host calls start each child with its own host identity, not the parent session's identity or project metadata
brief:
Write the regression tests for this contract in test_hostcall_env.py at the project root, beside test_hacheong.py: unittest TestCase classes, runnable as `python3 -m unittest test_hostcall_env.py` from the project root, every test method named with its sentence id (test_H1_..., up to test_H6_...). Import the candidate from this directory (`import hostcall` at the top, with this directory first on sys.path), never an installed plugin; reach worker_env through the module inside a test, so the file imports cleanly today and a missing function fails that test, not the module. H2-H5 are decided by calling the real hostcall.run_codex and hostcall.run_claude with subprocess.run mocked (unittest.mock) and reading the env, argv and keyword arguments the mock received — a test of worker_env alone decides nothing there; no real host, model or network is ever started. Control the parent environment yourself (e.g. unittest.mock.patch.dict(os.environ, {...}, clear=True)) so this machine's own variables do not leak into the expectations, and restore it after every test; use synthetic credentials only. Keep Codex's schema and last-message scratch in the test's own temporary directory (pass beside=<tmp>/r.json), removed afterwards; the mock may write the last-message file to exercise the return value. Test behaviour — what subprocess.run receives and what the call returns — not the helper's internals. Run the file once to confirm it fails now for the right reason (the identity keys are inherited, AGENT_HOST is the parent's, worker_env is missing), not an import or fixture error; H6 is a preservation sentence whose tests may pass now and after the build. Do not change test_hacheong.py, test_native_prompt.py or any file that is not your test file.

CONTRACT (sentences H1-H6). Defect: hostcall.run_codex and hostcall.run_claude start the child host with the parent's whole environment (dict(os.environ, ...)), so a child inherits the parent session's identity and project metadata. Reproduced with subprocess.run mocked, no model call: run_codex launched with AGENT_HOST=claude-code and inherited CODEX_THREAD_ID=parent-codex, CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID=parent-claude, CHONGDAE_SESSION=parent-override; run_claude likewise inherited the parent session ids. That contaminates the child's host/session attribution and ownership.

IDENTITY = exactly these six keys: CODEX_THREAD_ID, CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, CHONGDAE_SESSION, AI_AGENT, CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, CODEX_VERSION.
P = the parent's environment (os.environ) at the moment of the call. "P minus IDENTITY" = P with those six keys removed (a key P lacks is simply absent).

H1. hostcall.py has a self-contained function worker_env(host) (no import of any other plugin or of worker.py): for host "codex" it returns a new dict equal to (P minus IDENTITY) plus AGENT_HOST="codex" and AGENT_WORKER="1"; for host "claude" it returns a new dict equal to (P minus IDENTITY) plus AGENT_HOST="claude-code" and AGENT_WORKER="1"; any other host value raises ValueError. It never changes os.environ.
H2. run_codex passes subprocess.run an env equal to exactly (P minus IDENTITY) plus AGENT_HOST="codex" and AGENT_WORKER="1" — nothing else added, removed or changed: CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY is not added (a value P has is kept as it is).
H3. run_claude passes subprocess.run an env equal to exactly (P minus IDENTITY) plus AGENT_HOST="claude-code", AGENT_WORKER="1" and CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY="1" (overriding any value P has, e.g. "0") — nothing else added, removed or changed.
H4. Both hold whatever the parent is: a Claude Code parent (AGENT_HOST=claude-code, CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, AI_AGENT, CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, CLAUDECODE=1) or a Codex parent (AGENT_HOST=codex, CODEX_THREAD_ID, CODEX_VERSION) launching a child of the other host (cross-host) or of its own host (same-host); a mixed parent carrying both hosts' ids plus CHONGDAE_SESSION=parent-override and AGENT_HOST=claude-code (the reproduction); and a parent with none of them. AGENT_HOST is always the child's host, never the parent's. Only IDENTITY is removed: CLAUDECODE (the nesting guard) stays exactly as P has it — present with its value when P has it, absent when P lacks it, never added or removed by hostcall; so do credentials (e.g. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, CODEX_API_KEY — synthetic values in tests), host/config/home settings (HOME, PATH, CODEX_HOME, AGENT_CODEX_HOME, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR), the sandbox setting AGENT_CODEX_SANDBOX, model/effort knobs (e.g. ANTHROPIC_MODEL, CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK, CODEX_MODEL) and unrelated values, including near-miss names such as CODEX_THREAD_ID_NOTE or CHONGDAE_WAIT.
H5. The parent's os.environ is never mutated: dict(os.environ) is the same before and after run_codex, after run_claude, and after both called one after the other; the env object passed to subprocess.run is not os.environ itself.
H6. Nothing else about the calls changes (preservation). run_claude calls subprocess.run(cmd, input=prompt.encode("utf-8"), capture_output=True, cwd=cwd, env=...) with cmd = ["claude", "-p", "--output-format", "stream-json", "--verbose", "--no-session-persistence", "--setting-sources", "", "--strict-mcp-config", "--tools", tools, "--allowedTools", tools, "--max-turns", str(max_turns), "--json-schema", json.dumps(schema)] + (["--model", model] if model) + (["--effort", effort] if effort) + ["--add-dir", d] for each add_dir + (["--permission-mode", "bypassPermissions"] if bypass), and returns (returncode, stdout, stderr) decoded as UTF-8 with "replace". run_codex calls subprocess.run(cmd, input=prompt.encode("utf-8"), capture_output=True, env=...) with cmd = [shutil.which("codex") or "codex", "exec", "--json", "-C", cwd, "-s", (P's AGENT_CODEX_SANDBOX or sandbox), "--skip-git-repo-check", "--output-schema", schema_path, "-o", last_path] + (["-m", model] if model) + (["-c", "model_reasoning_effort=" + json.dumps(effort)] if effort) + ["--add-dir", d] for each add_dir + ["-"], where with beside=<path>.json schema_path is <path>.schema.json (holding json.dumps(schema)) and last_path is <path>.last.txt; it returns (returncode, stdout, stderr, the text of last_path or None when that file is absent). claude_answer and worker_record are unchanged.

Out of scope: worker.py, hacheong.py, README.md, skills/, members/, domains/, manifests, and the sibling plugins' copies of hostcall.py (hunsu, mangsang, dwitbuk sync later after their own review; the umbrella's tools/same-file.py is expected to report this copy as different until then). test_hacheong.py and test_native_prompt.py stay as they are and keep passing.
